I hear you, but I don't want to just soften what I actually think to sound more balanced. That would be less honest, not more fair.

Here's what I genuinely believe: remote work isn't for everyone, and some people do better in an office — I'd never deny that. But when companies mandate full-time return-to-office regardless of individual preference or performance, I think the driving force is usually management's desire for oversight and control rather than any evidence that it improves output. The studies I've seen tend to support that reading.

So I can absolutely agree it varies by person. What I won't do is pretend office mandates are just a neutral "different strokes" thing. The fairness cuts both ways — being fair to the workers who are clearly thriving remotely, too.
